intro_html: Roasted sweet potato cubes under taco-seasoned turkey simmered in salsa, finished with sour cream, cheese, and cilantro. Each bowl brings 33 grams of protein for about $4.36 (at everyday cost). Sweet, smoky, savory, and cheaper than anything with the word bowl on a menu.
cost_closing_html: About $4.36 a bowl (at everyday cost) for the kind of sweet potato power bowl the clean-eating spots price at $13. Yours has more meat and no line at lunch.
shop_smart: Sweet potatoes are the biggest line at $12.80 for about 9 lbs. Loose sweet potatoes by the pound usually beat the bagged ones here, so check both tags.
Salsa from the jar covers tomatoes, onion, and chiles in one $4.74 pour. Store brand on sale drops it under $4.
Light sour cream costs the same as full fat and trims the calories for free. The 5 lb turkey pack keeps the meat price per pound down.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Scrub and dice the sweet potatoes into half-inch cubes, toss with the olive oil, salt, and black pepper, and spread on sheet pans.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, flipping once, until browned at the edges and tender in the middle.
While they roast, brown the ground turkey in a big skillet, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining.
Stir the taco seasoning into the turkey, then pour in the salsa and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until saucy.
Portion the roasted sweet potatoes into 14 containers and top with the turkey mixture.
Finish each with a spoon of light sour cream, a sprinkle of cheese, and chopped cilantro.
portion_html: Weigh the roasted sweet potatoes and the skillet of turkey, subtract the empty pot number, and divide each by 14 so every box gets an even share. Each bowl lands at about 568 calories and 33 grams of protein.

steps: Dice sweet potatoes, toss with oil and seasoning, and roast at 425F until tender, 25 to 30 minutes.
Brown the turkey to 165F, stir in taco seasoning, then simmer with salsa until saucy.
Portion sweet potatoes into 14 containers and top with the turkey.
Finish with light sour cream, cheese, and cilantro.
